post.caption: Henry VIII's pendant looked like a fake. In 2019, a metal detectorist found a gold pendant in a Warwickshire field. He had taken up the hobby only six months before. A British Museum curator first asked if it was costume jewelry, but tests confirmed it is Tudor, made of 24 carat gold. One side carries the linked initials H and K. The other shows a Tudor rose and Catherine of Aragon's pomegranate. The museum says it is only linked to Henry VIII. In 2025, it asked the public to help buy the pendant, and more than 45,000 people gave.
